matches.rationale: Finding 1 identifies a mathematical inconsistency in the cross-attention equations (Eq. 9) in Section 4.3.1, specifically noting that Q_vi K_ir and Q_ir K_vi are dimensionally invalid without the transpose on K. This directly implicates the same cross-attention mechanism described in gt_id 1, which concerns the swapped queries and problematic formulation. The finding detects a concrete defect in the same equations, satisfying R1 (same locus) and R4 (specific defect).

Finding 3 identifies that the loss functions in Section 4.3.2 (Eqs. 10-13) are not well-defined when applied to images with different channel counts (one-channel infrared vs. three-channel visible), without specifying how to handle this mismatch. This directly relates to gt_id 2's concern that the loss functions lack clarity about how they are applied to different modalities, creating optimization inconsistencies. Both point to the same underlying issue of underspecified loss application across modalities.
